name: ClickUp
verdict: Self-serve: a Workspace owner or admin creates the OAuth app under Settings → Apps, and no review or partner program was found. Likely 1-3 days; admin allow-list controls are unconfirmed.
needGuide: Short one: create the app as an owner or admin, add the redirect URL, ship.

auth.detail: Authorization code grant: authorize at app.clickup.com/api, exchange at api.clickup.com/api/v2/oauth/token. Access tokens currently do not expire and no refresh tokens or PKCE are documented (docs warn this may change; non-SSL redirects may be dropped). Users choose which Workspaces to authorize.

approval.gate: None documented: no review or partner program found for OAuth apps. Only Workspace owners or admins can create the OAuth app. Whether an App Center listing exists or needs review was not found.

scopes.why: No scope parameter; the token acts with the user's permissions in the Workspaces they choose.
scopes.summary: No scope parameter documented; the token acts with the authorizing user's permissions in the Workspaces they selected. No scope-based review.

cost: Free; API rate limits depend on the customer Workspace plan
prerequisites: Account and owner: A ClickUp Workspace owner or admin must create the app (docs); do it from a company-owned Workspace so the app is not tied to one person's seat.
Where you register: Avatar → Settings → Apps → Create new app → name + redirect URL → copy client_id and secret
Cost: Free; API rate limits depend on the customer Workspace plan

registerAt.path: Avatar → Settings → Apps → Create new app → name + redirect URL → copy client_id and secret

steps.do: Sign in as a Workspace owner/admin and open avatar → Settings → Apps → Create new app
Enter the app name and HTTPS redirect URL; copy client_id and client secret into a secrets manager
Implement the authorize redirect with a state parameter and the token exchange; store the non-expiring token encrypted
Call Get Authorized Teams (Workspaces) after consent to record which Workspaces were granted
Handle 429 using X-RateLimit headers (100/min on Free-Business, 1,000 Business Plus, 10,000 Enterprise)
Test with a second Workspace and a non-admin user; implement a re-authorize flow for changing Workspaces
Add token-expiry/refresh handling behind a feature flag in case ClickUp starts expiring tokens

roles.team: A ClickUp Workspace owner or admin must create the app (docs); do it from a company-owned Workspace so the app is not tied to one person's seat.
roles.customer: The authorizing user selects one or more Workspaces during consent; creating or approving may depend on their Workspace role. Admin controls blocking third-party apps not confirmed.

testing: Create the app in your own Workspace and authorize it into that Workspace or another you control.
Free plans are limited to 100 requests/minute per token.

blockers.fix: Enforce least privilege in your own agent layer and disclose it to customers.

blockers.problem: Tokens never expire, so a leaked token stays valid
blockers.fix: Encrypt at rest and give users a disconnect that deletes it.

blockers.problem: Low rate limits on Free to Business plans (100/min) can throttle an agent
Only admins can create the OAuth app
blockers.fix: Have an admin of your company Workspace do it.

automation.agentCan: Write the OAuth code, Workspace discovery, rate-limit handling, secure storage, and test calls.
automation.humanMust: Admin sign-in to create the app and any customer-side authorization by the end user.

uncertain: App Center listing or review process, any admin allow-list controls, PKCE/refresh plans, and test-Workspace options were not confirmed.
